findings.title: Legacy embeddable_hosts values are inserted without normalization
findings.body: The migration copies each line from the old embeddable_hosts site setting directly into embeddable_hosts.host. Existing values may include a scheme or path, but EmbeddableHost.record_for_host later parses the referer/embed URL and searches only by URI host. Rows such as `http://example.com` or `example.com/path` therefore will not match `example.com`, so hosts that were allowed before the upgrade can stop working.

findings.title: Unescaped values in migration SQL
findings.body: The INSERT statement interpolates the site-setting line `h` directly into SQL. A stored value containing a single quote can break the migration or execute unintended SQL. Use quoted/parameterized values rather than string interpolation.

findings.title: Migration assumes site-setting/category rows exist
findings.body: The migration calls `execute(...)[0]['id']` without checking whether a row was returned. On installations where `embed_category` was never changed, or where the uncategorized category setting row is absent, this raises NoMethodError and aborts the migration. The same pattern appears for `uncategorized_category_id` at line 15.

findings.title: Data migration is not reversible
findings.body: The migration uses raw INSERT/DELETE statements inside a `change` method. Rails cannot automatically reverse these operations, so rolling back the migration will raise an irreversible migration error. Use `up`/`down` or an explicit reversible block.

findings.title: before_validation crashes when host is nil
findings.body: The callback calls `self.host.sub!` without guarding against nil. Creating or updating an EmbeddableHost with a missing host value raises NoMethodError instead of returning a normal validation error.

findings.title: No uniqueness enforcement for host
findings.body: The model validates only the format of `host`; there is no uniqueness validation and the migration does not add a unique index. Duplicate host rows can be created, and `record_for_host` uses `.first`, making the selected category nondeterministic when duplicates exist.

findings.title: Hostname regex rejects valid modern TLDs
findings.body: The validation regex limits the TLD to 2-5 letters, which rejects valid modern domains such as `.solutions` or `.photography`. Admins would be unable to add real embeddable hosts that use newer TLDs.

findings.title: Port handling is inconsistent
findings.body: The validation regex permits stored hosts with ports, but `record_for_host` compares only `URI#host`, which excludes the port. A stored host like `example.com:8080` will not match requests to that port, while a stored host without a port implicitly matches all ports.

findings.title: Missing record handling causes 500 errors
findings.body: Update fetches the record with `.first` and passes it to `save_host` without checking for nil. Destroy does the same and calls `destroy`. A request with an unknown id raises NoMethodError instead of returning a 404 or error JSON.

findings.title: Unsafe assumption that params[:embeddable_host] exists
findings.body: `save_host` indexes `params[:embeddable_host][:host]` and `params[:embeddable_host][:category_id]` directly. If the request body does not include an `embeddable_host` object, the controller raises NoMethodError instead of returning a validation or parameter error.

findings.title: category_id is not validated against existing categories
findings.body: The controller assigns any supplied `category_id` and only replaces blank values with the uncategorized category id. It does not verify that the category exists, and it does not treat 0 as uncategorized. This can create embeddable hosts with dangling category ids, leading to missing categories in the UI and undefined behavior.

findings.title: PUT /admin/customize/embedding does nothing
findings.body: The update action renders the current embedding object but never applies or persists any parameters. The client controller has a saveChanges action that calls `embedding.update({})`; any future editable embedding attributes sent to this endpoint would silently not save.

findings.title: Edit action assumes host.category is present
findings.body: `this.get('host.category.id')` throws if `host.category` is undefined. This can happen when the category was deleted, the stored category_id is invalid, or the category is not present in the client-side category list. The component should use `host.category_id` or guard against a missing category.

findings.title: Client state after save can diverge from server
findings.body: After saving, the component sets `category` by looking up the local `categoryId`, but does not update `category_id`, and the lookup may return undefined. If the server coerces a blank category to uncategorized or the category cannot be found, the displayed row may show no category or stale state.

findings.title: Hydrating embedded ids assumes property is an array
findings.body: For keys ending in `_ids`, the code calls `obj[k].map` without checking that `obj[k]` is present and array-like. If a serializer emits null or omits the ids value for an empty relation, store hydration throws a TypeError. A guard such as `(obj[k] || []).map` is needed.

findings.title: No functional controller tests for new admin endpoints
findings.body: The specs only assert controller inheritance. There are no tests for create/update/destroy behavior, invalid parameters, missing records, invalid categories, duplicate hosts, or authorization. Given that these endpoints control which external hosts may embed the forum, this is a significant coverage gap.
